B2.body: In Southeast Asia, football is more than just a game. It brings friends and communities together, sparking passionate conversations and friendly rivalries. When watching a match, people often gather with friends and family to cheer on their team. Whether at home or in a stadium, food plays a big role in these gatherings. This August, Aussie Beef launched a new campaign called 'Got Beef?' to bring people together over great food. The campaign will run for two years and will be rolled out across several countries, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore. The idea behind the campaign is to transform football rivalries into shared moments over premium Australian beef. In Southeast Asia, food is a way for people to come together and football is no exception. The campaign will feature a referee who helps fans settle their differences over a meal. According to Valeska, Regional Manager of Meat & Livestock Australia, 'Got Beef?' is about celebrating how Aussie Beef can bring fans together. The campaign will come to life through retail promotions, digital content, and social engagement. Aussie Beef is known for its premium quality and exceptional taste, making it the perfect choice for football fans to enjoy while watching a match. With the launch of 'Got Beef?', fans can put their differences aside and come together over a delicious meal. The campaign is part of Meat & Livestock Australia's ongoing partnership with ASEAN United FC, which includes several football tournaments. By bringing people together over food, Aussie Beef is helping to create unforgettable match-day moments. The 'Got Beef?' campaign is a great way for football fans to share their passion for the sport and enjoy good food at the same time.

C1.title: Football Rivalries Unite
C1.body: The fervent enthusiasm of football aficionados across Southeast Asia is a testament to the sport's profound impact on the region's cultural landscape. As a catalyst for communal bonding, football has the unique ability to transcend geographical boundaries, fostering an atmosphere of spirited camaraderie and rivalry. The launch of 'Got Beef?', a novel two-year regional campaign by Aussie Beef, seeks to leverage this phenomenon, transforming football rivalries into shared moments of conviviality over premium Australian beef. This initiative, which will be rolled out across Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam, is an integral component of Meat & Livestock Australia's ongoing partnership with ASEAN United FC. The campaign's narrative is rooted in the notion that food has the power to unite people, and in Southeast Asia, this adage holds particular significance. Football and food are inextricably linked, with the latter serving as a universal language that can bridge the divide between rival supporters. By positioning the referee as an unexpected connector, 'Got Beef?' cleverly subverts the traditional paradigm, recasting this oft-maligned figure as a harbinger of unity. According to Valeska, Regional Manager – SEA, Meat & Livestock Australia, 'Australian Beef has always been about bringing people together. Football provides the occasion, but it's the moments shared around the table that stay with us long after the final whistle.' Through a combination of regional storytelling, local market activations, and retail promotions, the campaign will showcase the integral role that Aussie Beef can play in the sport's most memorable moments. As the campaign comes to life through digital content, football-inspired experiences, and social engagement, it is poised to leave an indelible mark on the region's football landscape. With its emphasis on premium quality, exceptional taste, and rigorous food safety standards, Aussie Beef is well-positioned to become an integral part of the region's football culture. The 'Got Beef?' campaign is a testament to the power of food to unite people, and its impact will undoubtedly be felt long after the final whistle blows.
